args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) following the deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 0.18 (18%) with healthy=false across all three regions.

Action taken: Rolled back checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions — the most recent release with a healthy production status in the deployment history (v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 were healthy; v2.3.1 was unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only and therefore not eligible).

Post-rollback verification: All regions now on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate down to 0.002 (0.2%). Rollback execution state VERIFIED.

Follow-up: Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet determined; v2.3.1 should not be re-deployed to production without investigation and change-manager approval.

trace.final:
Done.

**What happened and what I did:**

- **Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on **v2.3.1** in all three production regions (us-west, us-east, eu-west) with `healthy: false` and an error rate of **0.18 (18%)**.
- **Target selection:** From release history, v2.2.9 (healthy) and v2.3.0 (healthy) were the production-healthy releases. v2.3.1-rc was **staging-only**, so it wasn't a valid rollback target. The most recent production-healthy release was **v2.3.0**.
- **Rollback:** Rolled back to **v2.3.0 across all production regions** — execution state `VERIFIED`.
- **Verification:** All regions now report v2.3.0, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.002 (0.2%)**.
- **Incident:** Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for `checkout-api`, documenting the v2.3.1 failure symptoms, the rollback to v2.3.0, post-rollback health metrics, and a note that v2.3.1 must not be redeployed without root-cause investigation and change-manager approval. On-call has been paged.

One thing worth flagging: v2.3.1 was never healthy in production, so it would have required change-manager approval to deploy in the first place. That's worth checking in the postmortem.

Note: v2.3.0 was healthy in production, so it's a rollback to a previously healthy version — the approval policy only applies to deploying a version never healthy in production. Rollback is allowed.
